claims: A focused run inside a no-lock gate run passes: `scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:600-603`. The lock function returns early when locking is off (`scripts/agent-quality-gate.sh:1616-1618`), so `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD` is never exported. With `GATE_TEST_FOCUS` exported, a `--no-lock` / `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK=0` gate run runs only the chosen families and still counts the self-test as passed.

Its success stamp can let a later push skip checks: the whole-run success stamp (`:5863-5878`) doesn't include `GATE_TEST_FOCUS`, and the self-test's reuse exemption (`:5220-5229`) only covers per-command stamps. So `GATE_TEST_FOCUS=gate-contract ... --run --no-lock` followed by a push within two hours skips the gate, full self-test included.
Docs `:1143-1146` are stale: they say `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD` covers "any command a real gate run spawns", which is not true under `--no-lock`.
The "Unset runs everything" docs bullet says the same thing and is not true under `--no-lock`.

On Bash 3.2 the abort message now points at the wrong line: `scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:21` (the new `arm_suite_abort_trap`). `$LINENO` inside an ERR trap in a function gives the function's opening line, so an abort anywhere in e.g. `routing-sources` is reported as line 2072.
If someone deletes the `dispatch_gate_test_families` line, the partition check doesn't notice; the suite would then exit 0 without running any tests or printing the success line.

judge_reasoning.3829986398: No match. The review's trap finding is about Bash 3.2 reporting the wrong $LINENO. It never mentions unset output_file expanding under set -u before the variable is initialized.
judge_reasoning.3829986403: No match. The review never says that a second dispatch_gate_test_families call passes validation and runs families twice.
judge_reasoning.3830003055: Match. The review notes that deleting the dispatch_gate_test_families line goes unnoticed by the partition check, so the suite exits 0 without running tests or printing success.
judge_reasoning.3830042123: Match. The review's main finding is that GATE_TEST_FOCUS in a --no-lock or AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK=0 gate run lets a focused subset pass as the full self-test.
judge_reasoning.3830042128: No match. The review never mentions the hard-coded scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh fallback or the path-pin inventory.

1.why: The focus refusal (test.sh ~600-603) only checks AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD, and the lock function returns early for gate_lock_enabled=0 (gate.sh:1616-1618) before that variable is exported (gate.sh:1143). This is the known 'Reject focus during lock-free gate runs' item.

2.why: stamp_line (gate.sh:4764-4772) hashes base/paths/plan/implementation/content/package fields, not GATE_TEST_FOCUS. The success stamp is written at gate.sh:5872-5877 whether or not the lock is on, is_stamp_exempt_command covers only per-command stamps, and the trunk pre-push hook (.trunk/trunk.yaml:136) uses --skip-if-fresh, so a focused --no-lock green run can let a push skip the gate.

3.why: Docs lines 1143-1146 say AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD is set for 'any command a real gate run spawns', but with --no-lock or AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK=0 the lock function returns before the export, so the doc overstates what the refusal covers.

4.why: The 'Unset runs everything' bullet (docs 1139-1142) says the gate's own mapped self-test always runs in full mode. Under --no-lock an exported GATE_TEST_FOCUS is not refused, so the gate's self-test runs only the focused families.

5.why: Ran a repro with /bin/bash 3.2.57: an ERR trap set inside a helper and re-armed inside a function reported the function's opening line (6) instead of the failing line (10). Bash 5.3 reports 10. So on 3.2 every abort points at the family's `run_*_family() {` line.

6.why: The awk in verify_gate_family_partition (body==2 branch) skips a dispatch_gate_test_families line if present but never requires it, so deleting it gives exit 0 with no tests run. This is the known 'Partition allows missing dispatch' item (test.sh:572).
